\section{Notation}

All quantities refer to one run's post-onset window unless stated. The
table is complete; symbols not listed here do not appear.

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{$}l<{$}p{121mm}@{}}
\toprule
\tau & time since the identified onset, $\tau\in[0,\tau_{\rm end}]$ [s]\\
\tau_{\rm end} & window length; $x = C_2\tau_{\rm end}$ is its
  dimensionless form\\
\tau_i,\ N & the $N$ sample instants $0=\tau_1<\dots<\tau_N=
  \tau_{\rm end}$ (logging period $T_s\approx10$~ms)\\
y_i & measured roll/pitch rate at $\tau_i$, from the flight IMU
  [rad/s]\\
\omega_{\rm nom}(\tau) & nominal response
  $C_1(\cosh C_2\tau - 1) + C$ [rad/s]\\
C_1,\ C_2,\ C & amplitude $C_1 = K\Mdot$, exponent
  $C_2 = \sqrt{Wz_{CoM}/J_P}$, pre-onset baseline $C$\\
K,\ \Mdot & calibrated gain $K = 1/(Wz_{CoM})$ [1/(N\,m\,s)] and
  commanded ramp rate [N\,m/s]\\
W,\ z_{CoM},\ J_P & weight [N], CoM height [m], pivot-axis inertia
  [kg\,m$^2$]; $J_P = 1/(KC_2^2)$\\
e_\omega(\tau) & deviation of the true (noise-free) rate from
  $\omega_{\rm nom}$ [rad/s]\\
n_i & in-window disturbance: everything in $y$ that is neither
  $\omega_{\rm nom}$ nor $e_\omega$ [rad/s]\\
u_i & regressor $u_i = \cosh C_2\tau_i - 1$;\quad
  $\tilde u_i = u_i - \bar u$ its centred form\\
V,\ A,\ P & fitted family's span $V=\operatorname{span}\{u,\mathbf 1\}$;
  $A = [\,u\ \ \mathbf 1\,]$; projector $P = A(A^\top\! A)^{-1}A^\top$,
  in closed form $P_{ij} = 1/N + \tilde u_i\tilde u_j/\sum_k\tilde
  u_k^2$\\
\hat r & minimiser residual $\hat r = (I-P)\,y$: the per-run fit with
  $C_2$ pinned and $(C_1, C)$ free is exactly this projection\\
M & the fitted family $\{a\,u + c\,\mathbf 1 : a, c\in\mathbb R\}$, so
  that $\hat r = \min_{g\in M}$ in norm and $M$'s span is $V$\\
\hat n & calibrated estimate of $\rms(n)$, eq.~(T.9); distinct from the
  envelope built on $\kappa_b$\\
\rho(s) & deviation forcing at time $s$: the gravity remainder
  $Wz_{CoM}(\sin\varphi - \varphi)$ plus the ground-effect terms,
  evaluated on the true trajectory [N\,m]\\
\rbar & a priori pointwise bound $|\rho(s)|\le\rbar$ from the
  $10^\circ$ box, as in (93) [N\,m]\\
k_j & kernel column: response of $e_\omega$ at the samples to a unit
  impulse of $\rho$ at $\tau_j$, i.e.\
  $k_j(\tau_i) = \Delta s_j\cosh\!\big(C_2(\tau_i-\tau_j)\big)/J_P$ for
  $\tau_i\ge\tau_j$, else $0$; $\Delta s_j$ the trapezoidal quadrature
  weight [s]\\
\Phi & a priori bound on $\rms\big((I-P)\,e_\omega\big)$, eq.~(T.4)
  [rad/s, reported in $^\circ$/s]\\
E(\tau) & the pointwise envelope of (93),
  $E = \rbar\sinh(C_2\tau)/(J_PC_2)$; note
  $E(\tau) = \rbar\sum_j |k_j(\tau)|$ --- the same kernel without the
  projection\\
n_{\rm hi} & the part of $\hat r$ above $f_c = 5$~Hz; attributable to
  disturbance because the family and $e_\omega$ are smooth on the
  window scale\\
\kappa & spectral shape ratio $\rms({<}f_c)/\rms({>}f_c)$ of a
  disturbance record\\
\kappa_q & $\kappa$ measured on the run's quiet stretch of equal
  length, ending at the excitation start\\
\kappa_{\rm imp} & in-window implied ratio
  $\sqrt{\rms(\hat r)^2 - \rms(n_{\rm hi})^2}\,/\,\rms(n_{\rm hi})$\\

  $s_{\rm med} = \operatorname{med}(\kappa_{\rm imp}/\kappa_q)$;
  campaign constant $\kappa_b = s_{\rm med}\,\max_{\rm runs}\kappa_q$\\
\beta,\ \delta e_\omega & witness coefficient and remainder of Sec.~7:
  $\delta e_\omega = e_\omega - \beta\sinh(C_2\tau)$ with $\beta$

  trapezoidal end weights where integrals are quoted)\\

\section{The residual sees only what the family cannot absorb}

The per-run fit holds $C_2$ at its physical value and minimises over
$(C_1, C)$, which is linear least squares on $A$: the fitted curve is
$Py$ and the residual is $\hat r = (I-P)y$. The record decomposes as
$y = \omega_{\rm nom} + e_\omega + n$, and $\omega_{\rm nom}\in V$
exactly (it is $C_1 u + (C_1\cdot 0 + C)\mathbf 1$ evaluated at the same
pinned $C_2$), so $(I-P)\,\omega_{\rm nom} = 0$ and
\begin{equation}
  \hat r \;=\; (I-P)\,(e_\omega + n).
  \tag{T.1}
\end{equation}
This is Lemma~2 of the manuscript's Appendix~C, eq.~(C3), and its
proof there ((C8)) is the annihilation just described; everything in
this document builds on that identity, and the pointwise chain
(C4)--(C6) with the constants $\lambda_E$ and $\kappa$ is retained
unchanged. Where this document goes further is the \emph{model} term:
Appendix~C's Lemma~3 charges the projection through the envelope,
$D_i = \sum_j|P_{ij}|E_j$, while (T.4) below pushes the projection
inside the Duhamel superposition, where the family annihilates the
cosh part of every kernel column before the envelope is invoked at
all. Hence
\begin{equation}
  \rms(\hat r)\;\le\;\rms\big((I-P)e_\omega\big) +
  \rms\big((I-P)n\big),
  \tag{T.2}
\end{equation}
and this is where the old cap gave ground: it bounded the first term by
$\rms(e_\omega)\le\rms(E)$, the size of the deviation itself. But the
minimiser absorbs whatever part of $e_\omega$ lies in $V$, and most of
it does. That is not an accident of the data --- it is structural.
$e_\omega$ is built from the kernel columns, and a shifted cosh splits
as
\begin{equation}
  \cosh\!\big(C_2(\tau - s)\big)
  = \cosh(C_2 s)\,\cosh(C_2\tau) - \sinh(C_2 s)\,\sinh(C_2\tau),
  \tag{T.3}
\end{equation}
whose first part is $u + \mathbf 1\in V$ \emph{exactly}. What survives
the projection is only the $\sinh(C_2\tau)$ part, weighted by
$\sinh(C_2 s)$ --- small for impulses early in the window --- plus the
truncation of the kernel before its impulse time. Norm-weighted over
the columns, the family absorbs $68$ to $91\%$ of the kernel
($79.7\%$ in the median across runs) before any property of $\rho$ is
used.

Two objections deserve explicit answers, because both look fatal and
neither is.

\emph{First: $P\,\omega_{\rm nom}=\omega_{\rm nom}$ is an identity, not
an approximation.} The nominal is $C_1 u + C\mathbf 1$ built on the
\emph{same} pinned $C_2$ that builds $V$ --- both belong to the
estimator --- so the annihilation in (T.1) is exact by construction.
The exponent that can genuinely differ is the \emph{true} response's,
and that discrepancy lives in $e_\omega$ by definition; it is priced in
Sec.~3 below.

\emph{Second: the absorbed part has constant coefficients only per
impulse, and that is all the argument needs.} Aggregated, the Duhamel
integral reads
\[
  e_\omega(\tau) \;=\; \cosh(C_2\tau)\,A(\tau)
                    \;-\;\sinh(C_2\tau)\,B(\tau),
  \qquad
  A(\tau)=\tfrac1{J_P}\!\int_0^\tau\!\cosh(C_2 s)\rho(s)\,ds,
  \quad
  B(\tau)=\tfrac1{J_P}\!\int_0^\tau\!\sinh(C_2 s)\rho(s)\,ds,
\]
and $A$, $B$ vary with $\tau$, so $e_\omega$ is \emph{not} a fixed
combination of $\cosh$ and $\sinh$ and is certainly not in $V$. But
the projection is never applied to that aggregated form. It is applied
per impulse, by linearity: in each column $k_j$ the shift $s_j$ is
fixed, the coefficients $\cosh(C_2 s_j)$ and $\sinh(C_2 s_j)$ in (T.3)
are numbers, and the cosh part is annihilated column by column. The
$\tau$-dependence of $A$ and $B$ is precisely the running upper limit
--- the truncation indicator $\mathbf 1_{\tau\ge s_j}$ of each column
--- and that truncation is carried, not discarded: it is the second
surviving piece in $(I-P)k_j$, evaluated exactly in the numerical
$\Phi$. Measured on the exact nonlinear $e_\omega$, the projection
absorbs $61$ to $67\%$ of it in RMS across the rates, and the
surviving $0.065$--$0.078^\circ$/s correlates $-0.5$ to $-0.65$ with
$(I-P)\sinh(C_2\tau)$ --- the sinh component and the truncation,
exactly as the column split predicts.

\section{The model term $\Phi$}

By Duhamel on the deviation dynamics
$J_P\ddot e_\varphi = Wz_{CoM}\,e_\varphi + \rho$ (with
$e_\varphi(0)=\dot e_\varphi(0)=0$; $e_\omega = \dot e_\varphi$), the
sampled deviation is $e_\omega = \sum_j \rho(\tau_j)\,k_j$ to
quadrature accuracy. Linearity of $I-P$, the triangle inequality
applied pointwise, and $|\rho|\le\rbar$ give
\begin{equation}
  \big|\big[(I-P)\,e_\omega\big]_i\big|
  \;\le\; \rbar\sum_j\big|\big[(I-P)\,k_j\big]_i\big|
  \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
  \rms\big((I-P)e_\omega\big)\;\le\;\Phi
  \;=\;\rbar\,\Big\|\textstyle\sum_j\big|(I-P)k_j\big|\Big\|_{\rms},
  \tag{T.4}
\end{equation}
computable a priori from $(C_2, J_P, \rbar)$ and the sample grid alone.
Without the projection the same construction returns exactly the old
envelope, $\rbar\sum_j|k_j(\tau)| = E(\tau)$, so the ratio
$\rms(E)/\Phi$ isolates what absorption is worth: a factor $12$ at
$\Mdot=0.10$~N\,m/s falling to $4$ at $1.20$, with
$\Phi = 0.40$ down to $0.26^\circ$/s.

Both the representation and the bound were verified on the exact
nonlinear tip-over: the kernel sum reconstructs $e_\omega$ to
$3\times10^{-4}\,{}^\circ$/s, and the realised
$\rms\big((I-P)e_\omega\big)$ is $0.065$--$0.078^\circ$/s across the
rates --- inside $\Phi$ with a factor $4$ to $5$ to spare, of which
about $2$ is $\rbar$ against the realised $|\rho|$ and about $2$ is the
sign coherence the triangle step discards.

\paragraph{If the pinned exponent mis-states the true one.} Let the
true response carry $C_2^* = (1+\varepsilon_2)C_2$. Whichever nominal
one chooses to name, the correction is the same vector: with the
calibrated nominal, the mismatch joins $e_\omega$; with the true-exponent
nominal, the annihilation fails by $(I-P)(\omega^* - \omega_{\rm nom})$
--- and since $(I-P)\omega_{\rm nom}=0$, both bookkeepings add
identically
\begin{equation}
  \Phi_{\varepsilon_2}
  \;=\;|\varepsilon_2|\,
  \big\|(I-P)\,\big[C_1 C_2\tau\sinh(C_2\tau)\big]\big\|_{\rms}
  + O(\varepsilon_2^2),
  \tag{T.4$'$}
\end{equation}
the first-order response to a relative exponent error, projected. On
the campaign grids this is $0.018$--$0.022^\circ$/s per $1\%$ of
$\varepsilon_2$ --- $5$--$7\%$ of $\Phi$ --- flat across the rates:
even $\varepsilon_2 = 5\%$ costs about $0.1^\circ$/s against a cap
margin of $0.6$--$0.9$. Since $C_2$ is itself fitted from the data by
the stage-one PNLS with the exponent free, $\varepsilon_2$ at the few-percent
level is what the calibration residuals allow, and the term is carried
for completeness rather than out of need.

\section{The noise term}

Projections contract, so $\rms\big((I-P)n\big)\le\rms(n)$, and the task
is an estimate of $\rms(n)$ that does not use the residual being
bounded. Its high-frequency part needs no estimation:
above $f_c = 5$~Hz the family and $e_\omega$ are smooth on the window
scale and can contribute nothing --- and by (T.4) their total
contribution anywhere is at most $\Phi$ --- so $n_{\rm hi}$ is measured
directly from the record. The low-frequency part is extended from it by
a spectral shape ratio: $\rms(n) = \rms(n_{\rm hi})\sqrt{1+\kappa^2}$
for the in-window $\kappa$.

The campaign fixes $\kappa$'s scale but not its per-run value. On the
$113$ runs with a quiet stretch of equal window length,
$\kappa_q$ runs $0.15$ (p10) to $1.31$ (max), median $0.37$, and,
decisively, $\kappa_q$ does not predict the in-window ratio run by run
(Pearson $r = 0.04$, $p = 0.70$). A per-run noise model is therefore
not available, and the bound uses the campaign envelope --- measured
entirely outside the windows it will be tested on:
\begin{equation}
  \kappa_b \;=\; \max_{\rm runs}\kappa_q \;=\; 1.31,
  \qquad \sqrt{1+\kappa_b^2} \;=\; 1.65.
  \tag{T.5}
\end{equation}

\section{The bound, on the campaign}

\begin{equation}
  \boxed{\;\rms(\hat r)\;\le\;\Phi
  \;+\;\rms(n_{\rm hi})\,\sqrt{1+\kappa_b^2}\;}
  \tag{T.6}
\end{equation}

per run, with $\Phi$ from (T.4) and the run's own measured
$n_{\rm hi}$. On the $140$ runs (means over the $20$ at each rate):

$^\circ$/s & & \\
\midrule

It holds on every run --- per-run used fraction p10 $0.49$, median
$0.56$, p90 $0.68$, worst $0.82$ --- it is below the old cap at every
rate, and it is \emph{flat}: the cap runs $1.66$ to $1.87^\circ$/s
across a twelvefold change in ramp rate, matching the flat residual,
where the old cap fell $5.77$ to $1.98$.

Little of the remaining width is removable within this form. The
binding run fixes the smallest admissible cap factor at $1.28$ (against
the $1.65$ in use), and even at that untenable limit --- it is set by
the very run it must cover --- the mean used fraction only reaches
$0.70$. The distance from $0.58$ to that ceiling is the price of
covering the worst spectral shape in the campaign with one constant.

\section{What the bound says, and what it cannot}

Applying (T.4) to (T.1) two-sidedly gives
\begin{equation}
  \big|\,\rms(\hat r) - \rms\big((I-P)n\big)\,\big| \;\le\; \Phi ,
  \tag{T.7}
\end{equation}
so the residual \emph{is} the projected disturbance to within
$0.26$--$0.40^\circ$/s. That is the flatness of Fig.~\ref{fig:tight-rms}
read as a theorem: the residual does not depend on $\Mdot$ because the
disturbance floor does not, and the model error, whose bound does fall
with the rate, is capped at a third of the residual's size in the
median --- $11\%$ of its power. The same statement fixes the limit of
this check:
a residual test can confirm $\rho$'s contribution is below $\Phi$, but
it cannot resolve $\rho$ inside the disturbance floor. The instrument
that tests $\rho$ is the forward check of (108), which propagates each
perturbation along the measured trajectory and is not noise-limited.

\section{The same bound by optimality alone, evaluated at the theory
values}

The two-line argument needs no projector at all:
\begin{equation}
  \rms(\hat r) \;=\; \min_{g\in M}\rms(y-g)
  \;\le\; \rms(e_\omega + n)
  \;\le\; \rms(e_\omega) + \rms(n),
  \tag{T.8}
\end{equation}
valid because $\omega_{\rm nom}\in M$ (same pinned $C_2$; freeing $C_2$
as well would only lower the left side). This is the old (VIII.3);
what made its cap loose was never the argument but the numbers put into
it. Putting in tight ones:

\emph{The model term at its theory value.} Instead of the Chebyshev
envelope $\rms(E) = 4.88$ down to $1.12^\circ$/s, take
$\rms(e_\omega)$ itself from the forward-integrated exact tip-over ---
the same machinery the forward check of (108) rests on:
$0.236$ down to $0.165^\circ$/s across the rates.

\emph{The noise term at its calibrated estimate.} Instead of the
worst-case envelope of (T.5), take the middle of the distribution:
\begin{equation}
  \hat n \;=\; \rms(n_{\rm hi})\,
  \sqrt{1+\big(s_{\rm med}\,\kappa_q\big)^2},
  \tag{T.9}
\end{equation}
each run's own hi-band content, extended by its own quiet-window shape
ratio times the campaign-median in-window enhancement ($\kappa_q$
replaced by its campaign median $0.37$ on the $27$ runs without a quiet
stretch).

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.86\linewidth]{fig_opt_rms.png}
\caption{(T.8) with both terms at their theory values, means over the
twenty runs per rate with $95\%$ $t$ intervals. The stacked bar is
$\rms(e_\omega)^{\rm theory} + \hat n$; the green bar is the measured
residual; the open diamond is the quadrature prediction
$\sqrt{\rms(e_\omega)^2 + \hat n^2}$, which lands within $1$ to $12\%$
of the residual at every rate. The used fraction is $0.76$ to $0.85$
and the mean cap covers the mean residual at all seven rates; per run
it covers $126$ of $140$, the exceedances being the $\kappa$ scatter
that (T.9), an estimate, does not envelope.}
\label{fig:opt-rms}
\end{figure}

The result (Fig.~\ref{fig:opt-rms}): the cap runs $1.20$ to
$1.30^\circ$/s against a measured $0.95$ to $1.08$ --- used $0.76$ to
$0.85$, covering the mean at every rate and $126$ of $140$ runs
individually. The rest of the gap is not looseness to hunt down; it is
the triangle step itself. Expanding the middle member of (T.8),
$\rms(e+n)^2 = \rms(e)^2 + 2\langle e,n\rangle/N + \rms(n)^2$, and the
cross term averages to zero for a disturbance uncorrelated with the
deviation, so the \emph{prediction} for the residual is the quadrature
sum $\sqrt{\rms(e_\omega)^2 + \hat n^2}$. Measured against the
campaign it lands within $1$ to $12\%$ of the residual at every rate
(the small excess being $\hat n$'s own margin and the two degrees of
freedom the fit removes). The summed form exceeds it by exactly the
triangle slack, at most $2\,\rms(e)\,\rms(n)$ inside the square, about
$0.19^\circ$/s here.

The division of labour between the two routes is then clean. This
section's evaluation is \emph{nearly equal} to the data --- used
$0.76$--$0.85$, prediction within $12\%$ --- because both terms sit at
the middle of their distributions; the price is that it is an
evaluation, and $14$ runs exceed it. The $\kappa_b$/$\Phi$ version of
(T.6) is the \emph{guarantee} --- it envelopes and holds on all $140$
--- at the price of the worst-case factor. One number cannot be both;
the pair brackets the residual from the middle and from above.

\section{A kernel-free bound: witness and maximum principle}

Every tightened route so far computes the kernel columns and the
projector. This section derives a bound that computes \emph{neither} ---
closed-form constants only --- yet stays flat across the rates, and is
evaluable before the experiment.

\emph{Step 1: a witness.} The minimiser beats every member of the
family, so it suffices to exhibit one member and measure the distance
to it. Take
\begin{equation}
  \hat h \;=\; \omega_{\rm nom} + \beta\sinh(C_2\tau),
  \qquad
  \beta \;=\; \frac{e_\omega(\tau_{\rm end})}{\sinh(C_2\tau_{\rm end})},
  \tag{T.10}
\end{equation}
admissible by the shift identity of Sec.~2 ($\beta/C_1\approx0.04$ on
the campaign; $\sinh$ is the first-order onset-shift direction, so this
witness is ``the nominal with its onset nudged''). The value of $\beta$
is never computed --- the argmin inequality needs only that such a
member exists. The remainder
$\delta e_\omega = e_\omega - \beta\sinh(C_2\tau)$ then vanishes at
\emph{both} window ends: at $\tau=0$ because $e_\omega$ and $\sinh$
both start at zero, at $\tau_{\rm end}$ by the choice of $\beta$.

\emph{Step 2: the remainder solves a two-point boundary-value problem.}
Differentiating the deviation dynamics once,
$\ddot e_\omega - C_2^2 e_\omega = \dot\rho/J_P$, and $\sinh$ is a
homogeneous solution, so
\begin{equation}
  \ddot{\delta e}_\omega - C_2^2\,\delta e_\omega
  \;=\; \dot\rho/J_P,
  \qquad
  \delta e_\omega(0) = \delta e_\omega(\tau_{\rm end}) = 0 .
  \tag{T.11}
\end{equation}

\emph{Step 3: maximum principle.} The operator
$v\mapsto\ddot v - C_2^2 v$ admits a maximum principle, so comparison
with the constant-forcing solution
$v_1 = \big(1-\cosh(C_2(\tau-\tfrac{\tau_{\rm end}}2))/
\cosh(\tfrac{x}2)\big)/C_2^2$ gives, with the identity
$J_PC_2^2 = Wz_{CoM}$,
\begin{equation}
  \big|\delta e_\omega(\tau)\big|
  \;\le\; \Big(1-\operatorname{sech}\tfrac{x}{2}\Big)\,
  \frac{\sup|\dot\rho|}{Wz_{CoM}}
  \;<\; \frac{\sup|\dot\rho|}{Wz_{CoM}} .
  \tag{T.12}
\end{equation}
No exponential appears. The causal envelope $E$ carries $\sinh(C_2\tau)$
because an initial-value problem lets the unstable mode grow; pinning
\emph{both} ends removes that mode, and the pinning is exactly what the
family's onset freedom provides. This is the differential-equation form
of ``the fit absorbs the growing part.''

\emph{The forcing rate, channel by channel.} Differentiating the same
remainders that build $\rbar$:
\[
  \sup|\dot\rho| \;\le\;
  \underbrace{\big(W l_{\rm arm}\,\varphi_{\max}
  + Wz_{CoM}\,\tfrac{\varphi_{\max}^2}{2}\big)\,\omega_{\max}}_{
  \dot\rho_2\ \text{(decays like } e^{2C_2(s-\tau_{\rm end})})}
  \;+\;
  \underbrace{|\beta_M|\big(\Mdot\,\varphi_{\max}
        + \Delta M_{\rm win}\,\omega_{\max}\big)}_{
  \dot\rho_1\ \text{(decays like } e^{C_2(s-\tau_{\rm end})})},
\]
with $\omega_{\max} = K\Mdot\sinh x$ the nominal peak rate. Everything
here is known \emph{before the experiment}: $W$ and $z_{CoM}$ from the
scale, $J_P$ from CAD, $l_{\rm arm}$ from geometry, $\varphi_{\max}$
the design box, $\beta_M$ from the ground-effect model, $\Mdot$ and the
window from the protocol. With a gyro noise figure for the second term,
the whole cap is computable before a single run is flown.

\emph{Step 4: shape the comparison, still in closed form.} (T.12)
prices the forcing at its supremum across the whole window, but
$\dot\rho$ is a product of responses that each grow like
$e^{C_2 s}$: the arm and gravity channels decay backwards from the
window end like $e^{2C_2(s-\tau_{\rm end})}$, the ground-effect
channels like $e^{C_2(s-\tau_{\rm end})}$ (measured on the exact
solution, the worst violation of these shapes is $2.6\%$; a safety
factor $1.05$ is carried on $\dot\rho_2$). Solving the same Dirichlet
problem with these shaped forcings --- elementary functions only ---
gives
\begin{equation}
  \big|\delta e_\omega\big|
  \;\le\; \frac{M_2(x)\,\dot\rho_2 + M_1(x)\,\dot\rho_1}{Wz_{CoM}},
  \qquad
  M_2(x)\to\tfrac1{12},\quad M_1(x)\to\tfrac1{2e},
  \tag{T.13}
\end{equation}
where $M_2$ is the peak of
$\tfrac13\big[e^{2u} - \sinh(u{+}x)/\sinh x
- e^{-2x}\sinh(-u)/\sinh x\big]$ over $u\in[-x,0]$ and $M_1$ that of
$\tfrac12\big[(u{+}x)e^{u} - x\sinh(u{+}x)/\sinh x\big]$ (the
$e^{C_2 s}$ forcing is resonant with the operator, whence the $1/2e$).
Replacing $(1-\operatorname{sech}\tfrac x2)\approx1$ by
$M_2\approx1/12$ is worth a factor of eight, and it is the
maximum-principle analogue of the reduction factors $1/7$ and $1/5$:
the forcing is largest exactly where the Dirichlet kernel, pinned at
the boundary, is smallest.

\emph{Step 5: the pre-onset segment the shifted witness leaves behind.}
The witness is, by the shift identity, a branch whose onset sits at
$\delta t_c = \operatorname{artanh}(\beta/C_1)/C_2$; on the piecewise
model the segment between the two onsets has the fit on its baseline
while the true branch has begun to rise, and that mismatch must be
charged. It is second order in $\beta$, and $\beta$ has the a priori
bound $\beta \le \rbar/(J_PC_2)$ (the envelope at the window end over
$\sinh x$), so
\begin{equation}
  \Delta_{\rm pre}
  \;=\;\sqrt{\tfrac{\delta t_c}{\tau_{\rm end}}}\;
  C_1\big(\cosh(C_2\,\delta t_c)-1\big),
  \tag{T.14}
\end{equation}
which is $0.08^\circ$/s at the slowest ramp and under $0.01$ above
$\Mdot=0.30$ --- carried, not neglected.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.86\linewidth]{fig_kernel_free.png}
\caption{The shaped kernel-free cap, (T.13) $+$ (T.14) $+\hat n$,
against the campaign; means over twenty runs per rate with $95\%$ $t$
intervals. The model term is $0.56$--$0.93^\circ$/s --- eight times
below the constant-forcing version (T.12) and at the level of the
projected $\Phi$ --- with no kernel computed and every constant
available before the experiment. All $140$ runs are inside at a used
fraction of $0.52$--$0.61$.}
\label{fig:kernel-free}
\end{figure}

On the campaign the model term (T.13)$+$(T.14) is
$0.56$--$0.93^\circ$/s and the cap holds on all $140$ runs at a used
fraction of $0.52$--$0.61$, per-run worst $0.83$
(Fig.~\ref{fig:kernel-free}) --- the same level as the $\kappa_b$
guarantee of (T.6), reached without computing a kernel column or a
projector entry. On the exact nonlinear solution the witness remainder
itself measures $0.16$--$0.17^\circ$/s, flat; the remaining factor
$\sim$$3$ is the design box $\varphi_{\max}=10^\circ$ against the
$4.8^\circ$ the runs actually reach, which is the price of stating the
bound before the experiment. Its place is therefore the \emph{protocol
design} role: predicting, before the campaign, the residual level
against which the fit-quality gate should be set --- and the flatness
of the measured residual is a property this construction predicts,
since nothing in (T.13) grows with the window.

\section{Provenance of every constant}

$C_2$, $K$, $J_P$ are the per-configuration calibration constants,
fixed before this analysis. $\rbar$ is a priori from the $10^\circ$
box, as in (93). The kernel, the projector and hence $\Phi$ follow
from those alone: the model part of (T.6) uses nothing measured in the
window. The noise part uses one campaign scalar,
$\max\kappa_q = 1.31$, from the quiet stretches only --- the bound is
built entirely from data outside the windows it is tested on.

One caveat is measured and stated rather than hidden. The in-window
spectra are heavier at low frequency than the quiet ones ---
$s_{\rm med} = \operatorname{med}(\kappa_{\rm imp}/\kappa_q) = 1.60$,
which is what pivoting on one gear edge adds --- so on $5$ of the
$140$ runs the residual exceeds the noise term of (T.6) alone, and it
is $\Phi$'s margin that covers them. A reader who wants the noise term
safe by construction can take
$\kappa_b = s_{\rm med}\times1.31 = 2.09$: that variant also holds on
all $140$ runs, at a mean used fraction of $0.44$, and prices the
in-window enhancement at about $0.6^\circ$/s of cap. The tight version
is reported as the result and the conservative one as the price of
removing its caveat.
